textGradientRow.reachedVia: a SgsColourPanel row declaring gradientCapable: true. Never mounted directly.

bannedLookalikes._note: ALL FOUR ARE AT ZERO LIVE INSTANCES as of 2026-08-19 (verified in src/blocks/*/edit.js). These are REGRESSION GUARDS, not a backlog. bannedLookalikes.matchRule: EXACT JSX-identifier match via Set membership, never substring. `MyColorPaletteButton` tokenises to a different identifier and must not flag. Any tag regex uses \b — multi-line JSX puts `<Component` at end-of-line and `[\s/>]` returns a false absence.

nativeUi._note: Bean's addition 2026-08-19: core's own colour UI is a fingerprint to detect and replace. It does NOT arrive via JSX — there are ZERO raw ColorPalette/PanelColorSettings mounts in any of the 83 edit.js files. It arrives through block.json supports.color, from which WordPress renders its own panel in the Styles tab.
nativeUi.detectVia: block.json supports.color — any sub-flag set true
nativeUi.conformantShape: declared with every sub-flag false (keeps __experimentalSkipSerialization while suppressing core's UI)
nativeUi.sequencingConstraint: Part O Cross-cutting A: the three-tab bar lands AFTER native-supports retirement, because while a block declares native color, core renders its own Styles tab regardless of what SGS does. DETECT NOW; retire per that existing plan, never ad hoc.
nativeUi.doNotDuplicate: Rule 24 (24-raw-canonical-component) already gates the JSX half. It never opens block.json, so this fingerprint does not overlap it.

states.minimumMeans: normal + hover. Bean ruling 2026-08-19: every colour row carries at least two states by default.

derivation.rule: A row's required state set = ['normal'] + the states DECLARED on its element in block.json supports.sgs.elements.<el>.states.
derivation.why: This needs no new vocabulary and no hardcoded 'is this a nav block' roster — the manifest already declares states per element, and Spec 35 FR-35-5 requires states be DECLARED, never parsed from attribute names (tabActiveTextColour renders as [aria-selected="true"], NOT :active; pauseOnHover/grayscaleHover contain 'Hover' but are booleans).

shapeRule.9a: ONE CONTROL SHAPE EVERYWHERE — a thin row carrying its swatches, showing how many states are pickable, picker in a popover.
shapeRule.9b: STATES LIVE INSIDE THE CONTROL — a tab toggle within the popover; never sibling controls, never a second panel.
shapeRule.9c: A COLOUR IS NEVER AN OPTIONAL ToolsPanelItem — not behind the '+' menu, not hideable per instance.

referenceImplementations.twoState: sgs/button — edit.js:381-470, one SgsColourPanel, 5 rows, all 2-state, 3 of 5 gradient-capable. The best 2-state+gradient example in the tree.
referenceImplementations.threeState: sgs/tabs — edit.js:176-199, tab-bg with normal/hover/active. The ONLY 3-state colour row in the entire library (measured 2026-08-19).

gradient.requiredMeans: Bean ruling 2026-08-19: UNIVERSAL, WITH DECLARED EXEMPTIONS. Every colour row must offer a gradient path unless its block.json declares an exemption with a reason. An absent gradient is a finding; a justified one is data.

mechanisms.how: a per-state gradient toggle inside DesignTokenPicker — the state carries gradientValue + onGradientChange, backed by a sibling {attr}Gradient string attribute
GradientCapableColourControl via a row declaring gradientCapable: true — text gradients need background-clip:text

<rowKey>.reason: <why this row has no valid gradient form>

exemption.rule: A reason string is REQUIRED and must not be boilerplate. An exemption without a real reason is itself a finding — same discipline as inspector-scan baselines (core/baseline.js hasRealReason).

gradient.blockedOnNothing: The gradient picker crashed every block until 2026-08-19 (fixed in daeec438 + 3fa0ebbd). The parked universal rollout is P-GRADIENT-UNIVERSAL-ROLLOUT.

qualifiesWhen._why: scope.eligible is DESCRIPTIVE and therefore SELF-FULFILLING: build-roster.py:106 computes surfaces.colour as `"color" in supports or an attribute named colour/color`, i.e. it is true exactly when the block ALREADY has colour. A block with none is excluded from this contract and can never be reported as MISSING a colour panel — only blocks that have some colour and got the shape wrong are visible. This predicate answers the other question: SHOULD this block have one? Added 2026-08-19.
qualifiesWhen._engineIsGeneric_predicateIsPerFamily: The engine evaluating this is shared; the evidence is not. Colour qualifies on painted surfaces; typography on rendered text; spacing on a box element; layout on multiple children; shadow on a card-like surface; link on an <a> or URL attribute. Each control type declares its own qualifiesWhen here rather than the engine growing a branch per family.

paintsOwnSurface.match: a CSS declaration of background, background-color, border-color or color
paintsOwnSurface.means: there is a surface for a colour control to govern

paintedByAncestor._note: ⚠ MEASURED 2026-08-19, and it changes WHERE the control belongs, not whether it exists. Every sgs/form-field-* block declares 4 elements (label/input/help/error) and paints ZERO of them; sgs/form paints all 52. So the field blocks qualify for colour COLLECTIVELY, and the control belongs on the ANCESTOR with children inheriting — the group-default pattern sgs/multi-button already proves (--sgs-mb-btn-*-default, D640). A predicate that only looked at the block's own stylesheet would wrongly report 13 form blocks as NOT-APPLICABLE.
paintedByAncestor.source: declared supports.sgs.elements with zero own paint declarations
paintedByAncestor.means: qualifies, but the control's home is the ancestor that paints it

featureParity.means: an SGS block replacing a core block must meet or exceed it (standing rule sgs-block-feature-parity-with-replaced-core), so if the replaced core block has colour supports this one qualifies

qualifiesWhen.verdicts: QUALIFIES + has a canonical panel = CONFORMANT. QUALIFIES + none = MISSING (real work). Does NOT qualify = NOT-APPLICABLE (not a backlog item, and must never be counted as one).

scope.eligible: roster.json blocks where surfaces.colour === true
scope.whyRosterNotDb: roster.json is in-repo, DB-derived, regenerated in prebuild and staleness-gated. The canonical DB lives OUTSIDE the repo and two 0-byte decoys sit inside it — a relative resolve lands on an empty file and passes clean forever.
scope.nullSurfacesRule: A block on disk but ABSENT from roster.json gets surfaces: null (core/roster.js:170,182), and reading .colour off it throws. An advisory rule that throws is SKIPPED, not failed (run.js:189-201) — it goes dark and green. Treat null surfaces as UNKNOWN, NOT CLEAN: emit an informational finding. Self-test cannot catch this (fixtures always get {}, never null).

altForUnboundedSet.note: A THIRD tier, out of this contract's scope — for a live/searchable/unbounded candidate set (a product catalogue, a post search), not a closed small enum. Recorded so a future reviewer doesn't mistake it for a segmented-vs-dropdown violation.

shapeRule._why: Spec 35 §3.1 names the threshold as the open gap this row exists to close.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v1: The FIRST version of this rule (flat 'optionCount<=5 AND every label<=14 chars') was WRONG — caught live by Bean looking at a real 5-option ToggleGroupControl screenshot (sgs/icon-list Marker Type: Icon/Emoji/Bullet/Numbered/None) where 'Bullet', 'Numbered' and 'None' visibly ran together. Root cause confirmed via live DOM measurement: ToggleGroupControl divides its available width EQUALLY by option count (at 5 options, each segment is only 47px), so the same label length that fits comfortably at 2 options does not fit at 5.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v2: The SECOND version (a strict px-per-character formula extrapolated from that ONE 'Numbered' data point — predicting only ~3-4 chars fit at 5 options) was ALSO too strict, per Bean's own live judgement after seeing it: 'I think 6 or 7 characters fits fine with 5 options.' A second real example confirmed this is the right read: sgs/container's 'Content band width' control (Normal/Wide/'Full (no cap)'/'Custom…', 4 options) shows 'Custom…' (7 chars, an intentionally-authored label with its ellipsis baked into the source text, not CSS truncation — confirmed by reading WidthPanel.js:29, NOT a bug) rendering CLEANLY with zero overflow, while 'Full (no cap)' (13 chars, two words) wraps to two lines. A single fixed px-per-character constant derived from one word ('Numbered') does not transfer cleanly to a different word ('Custom…') — real rendered text width varies per-character, not by a flat average. Rather than manufacture false precision from 2-3 data points, this row now states the rule as Bean calibrated it directly, with both confirming and refuting real examples as evidence.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v3: The THIRD and current version adds the LINE-COUNT ceiling Bean identified after seeing the deployed control: 'if the text also goes to 3 lines in a single box it should switch to the dropdown version too. In the example it's touching the top and bottom borders of the box.' v2 described 'Full (no cap)' as wrapping to TWO lines — that was an eyeball estimate and it was WRONG. Measured live 2026-08-19 via Range.getClientRects() on the real deployed control (the only method that returns true rendered line boxes; element height does not, because the span stretches to fill its segment): it renders THREE lines. That is the difference between 'a bit tight' and 'physically cannot fit', and it makes the rule mechanically checkable instead of a judgement call.
shapeRule.rule: Segmented (ToggleGroupControl) requires ALL THREE: (a) at most 5 options; (b) NO label renders on 3+ lines inside its segment (vertical overflow); (c) NO label's rendered line is wider than its segment (horizontal overflow). Any single label failing (b) or (c) forces SelectControl (dropdown) for the WHOLE control. Both are measured on the rendered control, not predicted from character count — character count only hints at the risk, geometry decides it. As a rough authoring guide, a short single unbroken word of ~6-7 characters reliably fits (confirmed live: 'Bullet' 6 chars at n=5; 'Custom…' 7 chars at n=4 with only 4px horizontal spare, so treat 7 as the practical ceiling).

twoDistinctFailureModes._why: ⛔ These are NOT the same defect and a detector checking only one will miss half the violations. Both of this contract's confirmed live violations were measured 2026-08-19 and they fail on OPPOSITE axes — a rule covering only line-wrapping would clear sgs/icon-list as healthy, and a rule covering only text width would clear sgs/container as healthy.

vertical_wrapsTooManyLines.cause: a MULTI-WORD label breaks at its spaces and stacks into 3+ lines, exceeding the fixed 38px segment height

shapeRule.howADetectorShouldCheckThis: Measure, do not estimate, and check BOTH axes in one pass. Element height/width are USELESS here — every segment span reports the full segment box (38px tall) regardless of what it contains, because it stretches to fill its slot; that is exactly what made an earlier 'two lines' reading wrong. Use Range.selectNodeContents(textNode).getClientRects(), which returns one rect per RENDERED LINE: `rects.length >= 3` is the vertical violation, `max(r.width) > segment.width` is the horizontal one. A static source-only detector CANNOT do this — wrapping and text width depend on font metrics, segment width and option count together, so it needs a real browser against the real rendered control. Not built this session; both known violations were found by running this measurement by hand.

Verified the family is real — 'typography' is declared in 25 block.json files (python enumeration of src/blocks/*/block.json supports keys, 2026-08-20). But the engine's supportFamilyFromDetectVia() regex (core/golden.js) only captures the FIRST dotted segment after `supports.` and axisNativeUi() only reads ONE level of sub-flags off that family (liveNativeFlags(supports[key])) — it has no way to check a SPECIFIC nested sub-flag like `typography.textAlign` in isolation from typography's other sub-flags (fontSize, lineHeight, fontWeight, textDecoration, etc). Declaring `detectVia: 'block.json supports.typography — any sub-flag set true'` here would fire on ANY typography sub-flag, not textAlign specifically — a false/imprecise VIOLATION any time a block enables e.g. fontSize support for an unrelated reason, and it would silently duplicate typography's own axis (which deliberately declares NO detectVia for exactly this family, per its own row, to avoid the same over-trigger). Proposed engine fix for the main agent, not built here (out of scope, core/golden.js is off-limits this session): a new schema shape, e.g. `nativeUi.detectViaSubFlag: 'typography.textAlign'`, paired with a new evaluator that reads `supports.typography.textAlign === true` specifically rather than the generic any-sub-flag-in-family check `liveNativeFlags()` already does. Until that lands, this axis stays honestly N/A (schema declares no READABLE native-UI competitor) rather than a forced, imprecise measurement.

Declaring `component: "AnimationControl"` here would not produce a partial/noisy signal — it would read MISSING/VIOLATION on all or nearly all 83 blocks despite the control genuinely being live and reachable in the editor for every eligible block, which is the same false-signal failure mode as an over-eager 80/83-conformant identifier, just inverted (near-universal false failure instead of false pass). Left undeclared; this is the AXIS-GAP case flagged below, not a fabricated identifier.

A block with a background Ken-Burns/parallax pair and no scroll-trigger animation at all would read 'conformant on animation', which is a false pass. Measurable, but not independently sufficient.
